title: TrainingRunConfig
description: The configuration record of one training run (ADR-010 section 5): seeds, generation size, model sizes, PPO settings and the worker's limits. Reviewed JSON in the repository, validated fail-closed and referenced only by the SHA-256 of its JCS bytes (CheckpointRecord.run_config_hash). Sizes and hyperparameters live here, never in code. League mixture and freeze-interval settings are added with the league scheduler (Wave 5).

lineage_id.description: Label of the lineage the run trains; every CheckpointRecord of the run carries it.

format_id.description: The Showdown format the games are played in.

seeds.description: Every seed of the run. None is a default: a run is identified by this record's hash.

run_key.description: Names the run in the battle seeds, the team draws and each Episode's collection record.

init_preview.description: Seed of the Preview network's random initialisation.

init_battle.description: Seed of the Battle network's random initialisation.

learner.description: Seed of the learner's own generator (minibatch order).

model.description: Network sizes (ADR-010 section 3): configuration, never code constants. d_model must be a multiple of n_heads (a reader rule).

options.description: Optional network options (ADR-010 erratum A4 item 2). Absent keeps today's bytes, hashes and checkpoints. A named option is added by the ticket of the experiment arm that needs it.

factored_preview.description: ADR-010 erratum A4 item 4. The Team Preview network scores an order as the sum over places of u(place, Pokemon token) plus v(lead pair) from the tokens at places 1 and 2, and does not use the cross-attention and interaction scorer for Preview. The candidate set, its order and the softmax over the real candidates are unchanged; the Battle network ignores it. Only true is a value (leave the key out for none). Layout changing: it changes the checkpoint tensor names and the checkpoint format.

shared_trunk.description: ADR-010 erratum A4 item 5. The Preview and Battle networks share one embedding and transformer trunk (role-specific candidate and value heads), trained by one optimiser over both networks' parameters. Each role's checkpoint is still a complete network and the two files hold equal trunk tensors. Only true is a value (leave the key out for none). Not combined with a warm_start that names the preview role (a Battle-only warm start gives its cloned trunk to both roles). Layout changing: it is part of the config and the checkpoint format.

separate_value.description: ADR-010 erratum A4 item 7. The value no longer shares gradient with the policy trunk. network: a second trunk and value head with no layer shared with the policy network (same encoder inputs and sizes, its own parameters). detached: the value head stays on the policy trunk but reads its output with the gradient cut. Layout changing: network adds tensors and both change the checkpoint format.

policy_output_scale_ppm.description: ADR-010 erratum A4 item 7. The scorer's last layer(s) start at this many millionths of their default initial weights (10000 is 1/100), so the initial policy is near uniform. Initial weights only: no tensor name changes, but it is part of the config and the checkpoint format. 1,000,000 is the default and is not a value (leave the key out).

games.description: Self-play games per generation: the frozen pair against itself.

baseline_games.description: Games against scripted baselines, at most one entry per actor (a reader rule).

excluded_abilities.description: Teams with a set holding any of these abilities are not drawn. A stop-gap for a known gap of the log-to-state reducer (Illusion's replace line, follow-up #851); a value of this record, not of the code, so it goes when the gap does.

max_turns.description: Turns after which the engine forces a tie.

n_parallel.description: Battles played at once against one worker.

handshake_timeout_ms.description: How long the worker may take to answer the hello.

max_line_bytes.description: Longest line of the worker protocol.

play.description: Optional (a minor change within v1, ADR-023 section 1, ADR-010 erratum A6 item 3, #1046): the play settings of the frozen pair's own seats. temperature_ppm is the sampling temperature in millionths: the pair samples softmax(logits * 10^6 / temperature_ppm) over the real candidates in self-play and baseline games, its behaviour_policy_id is the tempered pair's id, and the learner computes the old and new log-probabilities, the entropy, the approximate KL, the KL early stop and the anchor's KL (both policies) on the same tempered policy, so PPO stays on-policy. Absent means temperature 1 and today's bytes and run_config_hash; an explicit 1,000,000 is refused by the readers (one rule has one encoding, as in the policy query). The progress evaluation of a run that declares it adds this mode to argmax and temperature 1. A config that carries it is a new run from generation 0.

temperature_ppm.description: Play temperature in millionths, 1 to 999,999 (a reader rule refuses 1,000,000, the default).

search_labels.description: Optional (a minor change within v1, ADR-026 erratum E2 decisions 3 and 5, #1291): the frozen pair's own Battle move decisions are also LABELLED by the decision-time search after the game, from the stored Episode, into a separate label stream (labels.jsonl with its manifest label-set.json); nothing the search does is played or enters an Episode or the PPO stream. search_config_hash is the SHA-256 of the JCS bytes of the label search config (config/search/rerank-1-label.v1.json). An eligible decision (a Battle move request of the pair's own seat with two or more non-pending candidates) is selected when the first 8 bytes of SHA-256 over the JCS of {run_key, generation, game, player, request_seq, purpose: "search-label/1"}, read big-endian as n, satisfy n * 10^6 < label_share_ppm * 2^64. Labels start at start_generation. Comes with ppo.search_distill (both or neither) and needs warm_start, ppo.value_warmup (start_generation at least value_warmup.generations + 1), a team_dataset, and no opponent_sheet and no candidate feature set whose value reads candidate rows (probe-damage/1 and probe-damage-belief/1 are allowed). Absent keeps every byte and run_config_hash; a config that carries it is a new run from generation 0.

search_config_hash.description: SHA-256 of the JCS bytes of the label search config.

label_share_ppm.description: Share of the eligible decisions that are selected for a label, in parts per million (1 to 1,000,000).

start_generation.description: First generation whose games are labelled; at least ppo.value_warmup.generations + 1 (a reader rule), because a cloned value head is untrained until the warm-up ends.

ppo.description: PPO with GAE (ADR-010 section 1). Real-valued settings are integers in millionths (_micro) or billionths (_nano), because contracts carry no floating-point numbers.

clip_micro.description: PPO ratio clip epsilon, in millionths.

value_coef_micro.description: Weight of the value loss, in millionths.

entropy_coef_micro.description: Weight of the entropy bonus, in millionths.

normalize_advantages.description: Normalise advantages to zero mean and unit deviation within each role's batch.

target_kl_micro.description: Optional (a minor change within v1, ADR-010 erratum A1): after each complete epoch, if the arithmetic mean of that epoch's per-minibatch approximate KL (in minibatch order) is greater than this value in millionths, the role's remaining epochs of the generation are skipped. Absent means every configured epoch runs. A config that carries it is a new run.

learning_rate_schedule.description: Optional (a minor change within v1, ADR-010 erratum A1): the Adam step size per learner update. Absent or constant means learning_rate_micro for every update. Linear: with t the update index from 0, rate(t) = learning_rate_micro + trunc((final_micro - learning_rate_micro) * min(t, generations) / generations) in exact integers, truncating toward zero, so update `generations` and every later one use exactly final_micro. Both roles alike. A config that carries it is a new run.

entropy_schedule.description: Optional (a minor change within v1, ADR-023 section 3, ADR-010 erratum A6 item 4, #1048): the entropy bonus weight per learner update. Absent or constant means entropy_coef_micro for every update. Linear: with t the policy update index from 0, coef(t) = entropy_coef_micro + trunc((final_micro - entropy_coef_micro) * min(t, generations) / generations) in exact integers, truncating toward zero, so policy update `generations` and every later one use exactly final_micro (the rule of learning_rate_schedule). Both roles alike. With ppo.value_warmup t counts from the first policy update (the update after the warm-up), as the anchor's does, and the warm-up updates report entropy_coef_micro (the policy is frozen and the entropy term does not enter the value-only loss). Absent means no schedule. A config that carries it is a new run.

preview_bootstrap_micro.description: Optional (a minor change within v1, ADR-010 erratum A4 item 3, #1005): the weight w, in millionths, of the Battle network's value in the Team Preview step's return. The Preview return of an Episode is (1 - w) * game score + w * V_battle(first Battle decision of the same Episode), with V_battle the value the Battle network had BEFORE this update (both roles' frozen values are computed before either role is updated, so the Battle update cannot change the Preview targets); the Preview advantage is that return minus the Preview value. An Episode that has a Preview step and no Battle decision is refused. Absent or 0 means the game score alone (today's rule). Under ppo.value_warmup a warm Preview role trains its value head toward the same bootstrapped return. The Battle role is unchanged. A config that carries it is a new run.

value_warmup.description: Optional (a minor change within v1, ADR-019 section 4, #1111): for a run that declares warm_start, the first `generations` learner updates (generation 1 up to generation `generations`) train the value head only, on the cloned pair's own rollouts, with every other parameter of both networks frozen (the policy heads and the shared trunk stay byte-identical); update `generations` + 1 and every later one is normal PPO. The learning-rate schedule's update index counts the warm-up updates too. Absent means normal PPO from generation 1. A config that carries it is a new run.

generations.description: Number of learner updates, counted from generation 1, that train the value head only.

anchor.description: Optional (a minor change within v1, ADR-019 section 4, ADR-010 erratum A2 item 3, #968): for a run that declares warm_start, a KL anchor to the warm-start pair. Per decision, beta * KL(pi_theta || pi_anchor) is added to the loss, with both policies the softmax over the real candidates and pi_anchor the frozen warm-start pair (the declared checkpoints of both roles), computed once per generation from its frozen weights with no gradient. beta, in millionths, is kl_micro for a constant schedule; for a linear one, with t the anchor update index from 0, beta(t) = kl_micro + trunc((final_micro - kl_micro) * min(t, generations) / generations) in exact integers, truncating toward zero (the rule of learning_rate_schedule). Both roles alike. With ppo.value_warmup the anchor is inactive (beta 0) while the policy is frozen and t counts from the first policy update, the update after the warm-up. Absent means no anchor. A config that carries it is a new run.

kl_micro.description: beta at anchor update 0, in millionths.

search_distill.description: Optional (a minor change within v1, ADR-026 erratum E2 decisions 5 and 8, ADR-010 erratum A10, #1291): the Battle role's loss gains lambda * mean over the labelled decisions of a minibatch of KL(pi' || pi_theta), both over every real candidate (pending included, padding masked) at the run's play temperature tau (generation.play, else 1). The target is a function of the stored label alone: z(c) = ln(max(prior_ppm(c), 1) / 10^6); q_hat(c) = q(c) for a searched candidate and, for every other one, the prior-weighted mean of the searched q (weights prior_ppm); x(c) = (q_hat(c) - q_min) / (q_max - q_min) over the searched set; a label whose q_max - q_min is below min_spread_ppm is not used; pi' = softmax(z / tau + c_scale * x). Play-time truncation is ignored. lambda = coef_micro / 10^6 and c_scale = c_scale_micro / 10^6. The learner reads the label streams of the current and the previous aggregate_generations - 1 generations. Battle role only; under shared_trunk the gradient reaches the trunk. Comes with generation.search_labels (both or neither). Absent keeps every byte, report and hash; a config that carries it is a new run from generation 0.

c_scale_micro.description: c_scale in millionths: the logit gap the best searched candidate gains over the worst (4,000,000 is the ADR's 4).

min_spread_ppm.description: A label whose q_max - q_min (ppm) is below this is not used (0 keeps every label).

aggregate_generations.description: Label streams of this many generations (the current one and the previous ones) feed each update; at least 1.

team_dataset.description: Optional (a minor change within v1): the generated team dataset the generation loop draws its teams from. Absent means the interim pool of committed fixture teams. The directory is read by the dataset reader, which trusts nothing; the pool takes the dev and training splits, never validation. The dataset hash pins the manifest and every record: a directory that hashes differently is refused.

path.description: The dataset directory, relative to the directory the generation process runs in (the repository root for the loop driver) or absolute.

dataset_hash.description: SHA-256 of the JCS of {manifest_hash, splits: {dev, validation, training}}: the dataset manifest's own hash and, per split, the sorted record_hash list of the records the reader verified (empty training list for the committed layout). A swapped, added or removed record changes it.

warm_start.description: Optional (a minor change within v1; ADR-010 erratum A2, ADR-019 section 4): generation 0 is this declared pair of cloned checkpoints instead of the seeded random pair. The ids name checkpoints already in the run's checkpoint store (copied in by an explicit import command, never fetched). At run start each must hash to its id, hold the network of its role, and match the run's encoder version, engine-data hash and model section, and its CheckpointRecord must be a clone record (non-empty training_set_hashes, no parent, synthetic); anything else refuses the run. Generation 0 freezes the pair with no learner step, and the learner state starts fresh from the cloned weights. Naming battle alone (#1165) warm-starts the Battle role only: ppo.value_warmup and ppo.anchor then act on the Battle role only, and Team Preview trains as PPO from the first update. Absent keeps the seeded initialisation and today's bytes and run_config_hash. An older reader refuses a config that has it.

preview.description: Optional (a minor change within v1; #1165). Checkpoint id (SHA-256 of the safetensors file) of the cloned Team Preview network. Absent: Team Preview starts from the seeded random initialisation of seeds.init_preview, exactly as a scratch run's generation 0.

battle.description: Checkpoint id (SHA-256 of the safetensors file) of the cloned Battle network.

members.description: Learning members M (code bound 1 to 16; ADR-021 recommends a start of 4).

seats_per_member.description: Policy seats per member per generation, the unit the shares divide (ADR-021 section 3).

ladder_ppm.description: Current members, uniform, whole team pairs from both seats.

past_pool_ppm.description: PFSP over frozen snapshots of any member.

shares.description: Opponent shares of a member's policy seats, in parts per million; they sum to 1,000,000.

snapshot_every.description: Generations between snapshots of each member's frozen pair.

max_size.description: Cap on pairs in the pool (oldest evicted first, generation-0 pairs never).

max_past_per_member.description: Distinct snapshots drawn per member per generation (at most max_size).

floor_ppm.description: Least PFSP weight in parts per million, so no snapshot is starved.

window.description: Generations of results a strength is fitted on.

calibration_pairs.description: Pairs per anchor pair in the generation-0 anchor calibration.

ready_generations.description: Generations since a member's last copy before it may be replaced.

n_min.description: Least head-to-head pairs in the window for a copy decision.

margin_ppm.description: Margin above 500,000 the donor's one-sided lower bound must clear.

alpha_ppm.description: One-sided level of the bootstrap bound, in parts per million.

min_roots.description: Distinct generation-0 roots that must remain after a copy (at most members).

min.description: Lowest value the explore step may set.

max.description: Highest value the explore step may set (a reader rule requires min <= the starting value <= max).

min.description: Lowest value the explore step may set.

max.description: Highest value the explore step may set (a reader rule requires min <= the starting value <= max).

max.description: Highest value the explore step may set (a reader rule requires min <= the starting value <= max).

min.description: Lowest value the explore step may set.

max.description: Highest value the explore step may set (a reader rule requires min <= the starting value <= max).

bounds.description: Inclusive bounds the explore step clamps to; each must contain its starting value. target_kl_micro is allowed only when ppo.target_kl_micro is set.

clip_ppm.description: Clip fraction, in parts per million, above which a generation counts as unhealthy.

kl_ppm.description: Approximate KL, in millionths, above which a generation counts as unhealthy.

forfeit_ppm.description: Share of a member's games, in parts per million, that may be policy forfeits.

health.description: Health stops that quarantine a member (ADR-021 section 6).

reset_every.description: Generations after which an exploiter seat is reset (ADR-021 default 10).

member_ppo.description: Optional starting PPO overrides per member, sorted by member and unique; a field not given keeps the ppo value.

target_kl_micro.description: Starting ppo.target_kl_micro of this member (needs ppo.target_kl_micro).

population.description: Optional (a minor change within v1; ADR-021 sections 2, 3, 5, 6 and 8, ADR-010 erratum A3, #982): the run is a population of learning members on one ladder instead of one lineage. Every value is config data; code holds only the outer bounds (members 1 to 16, exploiters 0 to 2). Integers only; shares and thresholds are parts per million. Absent keeps today's single-lineage loop and its bytes and run_config_hash; a config that carries it is a new run, and the loop driver refuses it until the scheduler lands (slice 5). Reader rules (both readers): the three opponent shares sum to 1,000,000; min_roots is at most members; every explore bound contains its starting value (the member's override, else the ppo value; shares start from population.shares); past_pool.max_past_per_member is at most past_pool.max_size; member_ppo is sorted by member, unique, and each member is below members.

learner.description: Where the learner runs (ADR-010 section 4). A cuda run is not claimed to be bit-reproducible, and its hash differs from a cpu run's.

device.description: cpu, or cuda from the separate GPU environment (ADR-010 section 5.2); a missing device is refused, never replaced.

threads.description: Intra-op threads of the learner on cpu.

Encoder.description: Feature widths and scales of the encoder (ADR-010 section 3); part of encoder_version.

max_moves.description: Moves per Pokemon the encoder holds.

max_team.description: Pokemon per side the encoder holds.

max_picks.description: Team Preview positions an order names; at most max_team (a reader rule).

stat_scale.description: Divisor of a Pokemon's exact stats.

options.description: Optional encoder options (ADR-010 erratum A4 item 2). Absent keeps today's bytes, hashes and checkpoints. A named option is added by the ticket of the experiment arm that needs it.

candidate_features.description: ADR-022 tier A (ADR-010 erratum A5 items 2 to 4). Each damaging move part of a battle candidate also reads the rows of the engine's damage calculation on assumed opponent sets, which the Node side builds (PolicyQuery.candidate_features). Names the feature set; feature_set_hash is the identity hash the builder computes (mechanics config, assumed-set config, adapter format, reader, version manifest), so a pin bump or a config change is another set. Layout changing: it changes the encoder version and the checkpoint format. A pair that sets it has a policy id with a features member. probe-damage/2 (ADR-022 erratum E-22.3) also carries threat, speed and priority arrays, which the encoder attaches to the own and foe tokens and to the slot parts; probe-damage/3 adds belief_threats (damage of moves the opponent belief says a foe may hold), which the encoder folds into the threat rows with a belief flag and the inclusion. probe-outcome/1 (ADR-022 erratum E-22.5, slice H5) holds the five arrays of probe-damage/2 recomputed with the history facts declared, read exactly as probe-damage/2 reads them, plus outcomes (whether each own move part works now, per opposing-action branch), which the encoder pools per foe location and reads per branch in the move part; history_unknown is its own reason category.

candidate_matchup.description: ADR-022 tier B (ADR-010 erratum A5 item 1). Each move candidate also carries the engine-data type-chart cells of the move's type against the shown types of each opposing position and the ally, and a flag that the move's type is one of the user's shown types. Only true is a value (leave the key out for none). Layout changing: it changes the encoder version and the checkpoint format.

candidate_target.description: ADR-010 erratum A4 item 7. Each move candidate also carries the token of the Pokemon in the targeted active slot (the engine's target location read through the player's own request and the reduced slots; none for an untargeted or spread move, the user itself, or an empty or fainted slot), which the Battle network gathers into the slot part. Only true is a value (leave the key out for none). Layout changing: it changes the encoder version and the checkpoint format.

recent_history.description: ADR-010 erratum A4 item 7. The Pokemon and field features also carry the reducer's recent history from the player's own channel: per Pokemon the turns since its switch-in, its last move (through the move vocabulary) and target, the age and place of its latest action, the hit points it took and dealt this and last turn and its protect streak; on the field the turns since the weather, the terrain and each field and side condition began. Counts are scaled by the encoder's turn and stat scales and fixed divisors hashed into the encoder version. Only true is a value (leave the key out for none). Layout changing: it changes the encoder version and the checkpoint format.

history_facts.description: ADR-022 erratum E-22.5.4. The Pokemon and field tokens also carry the reducer's history facts from the player's own channel (history-facts/1): per Pokemon in play the move actions since its switch-in, the stall counter, hits taken, whether it was hurt and by which positions this turn, whether its last move failed, stat changes this turn, own moves used, volatiles held and their age; per Pokemon the berry it ate and the item it last used up; on the field each side's faints, the battle's last move and the remaining turns of pending slot effects. A fact the channel cannot settle is its own category or flag, never a guess. Counts are scaled by the encoder's turn scale and fixed divisors hashed into the encoder version. Only true is a value (leave the key out for none). Layout changing: it changes the encoder version and the checkpoint format.

exact_volatiles.description: ADR-010 erratum A4 item 7. Volatiles and field and side conditions are exact vocabulary ids (one column per id of the engine data: its conditions, moves, abilities and items) instead of SHA-256 buckets, and a Pokemon token also carries the types a typechange set. Needs a version 2 engine-data table; an id the vocabulary does not resolve fails closed. Only true is a value (leave the key out for none). Layout changing: it changes the encoder version and the checkpoint format.

opponent_sheet.description: ADR-027 slice 4, ADR-025 erratum E4: each opponent Pokemon token also reads its slot of the opponent sheet block, which the Node side builds from the opponent belief (PolicyQuery.opponent_sheet). feature_set is opponent-sheet/1 and feature_set_hash the feature set hash the builder computes (it names the belief identity, the k values and the rounding), so a new usage prior, belief config, reader change or pin bump is another set and a fresh run. Layout changing: it changes the encoder version and the checkpoint format.

Budget.description: Per-decision compute limits of self-play, in milliseconds.

Baseline.description: A share of the generation's games played against a scripted baseline (ADR-010 section 4). The baseline's seat never trains the policy.

actor.description: Which scripted baseline plays. damage-aware was added within v1 (ADR-018 section 7, a minor change): a reader older than it rejects a config that names it.

policy_id.description: The baseline's policy id, <name>@<commit>, as its Episodes record it.

final_micro.description: The entropy weight from policy update `generations` on, in millionths; 0 switches the bonus off.

generations.description: Policy updates over which the weight moves from entropy_coef_micro to final_micro.

final_micro.description: beta from anchor update `generations` on, in millionths; 0 releases the policy completely.

generations.description: Anchor updates over which beta moves from kl_micro to final_micro.

final_micro.description: The step size from update `generations` on, in millionths.

generations.description: Updates over which the rate moves from learning_rate_micro to final_micro.
